rounds.goodbye: The city can have you back now.
rounds.subtitle: The laptop is shut and the river is doing that thing it does at this hour — going copper, then pewter. Down to the greenway with everyone else who bailed on the gym, past the piers, into the wind that always has an opinion.
rounds.title: The River at Dusk

rounds.goodbye: In the door as it opens up. Elite timing.
rounds.subtitle: The radar says forty minutes and the fridge says you have nothing for dinner. Quick, then — over the footbridge, hit the greenmarket before the stalls start packing, one pause under the scaffolding to let the first fat drops miss you.
rounds.title: Before the Rain

rounds.goodbye: Beat the train. Obviously.
rounds.subtitle: The app said twelve minutes, then twenty, then gave up entirely. Fine — over the bridge under your own power, past everyone still staring at the countdown clock, faster than the shuttle bus and considerably smugger.
rounds.title: The F Train Is Down

rounds.goodbye: Nine a.m. can do its worst.
rounds.subtitle: For one hour the park belongs to the runners, the dogs, and you. In through the gate, up the drive with the hill everyone pretends isn't one, coffee at the end of it as a legally binding promise.
rounds.title: The Park Before Nine

rounds.goodbye: Okay. NOW home.
rounds.subtitle: You told yourself around the block. Then the next corner had better light, and the avenue was doing its sodium-amber thing, and the day still hadn't fully let go of your shoulders. One more block. Maybe two.
rounds.title: One More Block

rounds.goodbye: Worth both hills. It always is.
rounds.subtitle: They said 'come by around seven, it's a ten-minute walk.' It is two hills, and this city's ten-minute walks are load-bearing lies. Wine in your backpack, fog rolling over the ridge, calves filing a formal complaint.
rounds.title: Two Hills Over

rounds.goodbye: Two climates, one walk. Classic.
rounds.subtitle: The avenues are gray to the horizon, but the hill behind the house has a rumor of blue on it. Climb until the ceiling thins, then breaks — and there it is, the other city, the one that's been sunny the whole time.
rounds.title: Out of the Fog

rounds.goodbye: Quads: aware. Ego: intact.
rounds.subtitle: Between two ordinary streets there's a flight of stairs with someone's nasturtiums spilling over it, and at the top of it, another one. The city hides an entire vertical neighborhood for anyone willing to breathe hard.
rounds.title: The Secret Stairs

rounds.goodbye: The peaches were the plan all along.
rounds.subtitle: You need exactly nothing, which is why you're going. Along the Embarcadero with the bridge hanging in the haze, into the crowd of samples and small decisions, out the other side with peaches you didn't plan on.
rounds.title: Ferry Building Saturday

rounds.goodbye: The ocean will take it from here.
rounds.subtitle: Twenty minutes from your apartment the city just… ends, and it's all cypress and cliff and the Pacific being dramatic. The trail rolls along the edge, the bridge appears twice, and your phone stays in your pocket.
rounds.title: Lands End

rounds.goodbye: Lighter on the way down. That was the point.
rounds.subtitle: The stone steps start at the torii and don't negotiate. Up through the trees with the crows and the early joggers, coins in your pocket, whatever's been sitting on your chest all week ready to be set down at the top.
rounds.title: The Shrine Steps

rounds.goodbye: Home, eventually. As intended.
rounds.subtitle: The shortcut takes four minutes, which is exactly the problem with it. Through the backstreets instead — the yakitori smoke, the cat that owns the parking lot, the stepped alley up past the tiny bar that seats five.
rounds.title: The Long Way from the Station

rounds.goodbye: Still jet-lagged. Better at it now.
rounds.subtitle: Your body is certain it's yesterday afternoon. Nothing to be done but walk it — the intersection with no one in it, the vending machines humming their blue light, the first trains still an hour away and the whole city holding its breath.
rounds.title: Jet Lag

rounds.goodbye: Ninth seat. Photo finish.
rounds.subtitle: The place seats nine and the line starts forming at noon sharp, so at 11:40 you are already moving. Up the hill fast, ticket machine, the shuffle forward — twenty minutes of walking for a bowl worth forty.
rounds.title: The Ramen Line

rounds.goodbye: The river keeps going. You're allowed to stop.
rounds.subtitle: The river runs below street level like a secret, and the path follows it under the train lines. Every few minutes a bridge, every bridge a decision to keep going — past the izakaya glow and the office workers walking off their own days.
rounds.title: Along the Kanda

rounds.goodbye: Sunday, executed correctly.
rounds.subtitle: The Landwehrkanal moves at exactly the speed of a Sunday, and so does everyone along it. Under the lindens, over the bridge to the shady side, past the swans who have seen it all. The week can wait its turn.
rounds.title: The Canal

rounds.goodbye: Cleared for landing.
rounds.subtitle: They kept the runways and gave them to everyone. Kites, skaters, community gardens in old freight containers — and a horizon you can actually see. Walk the tarmac where the planes used to lift, into a headwind with no buildings to break it.
rounds.title: Tempelhofer Feld

rounds.goodbye: One record. It found you.
rounds.subtitle: You came for nothing in particular, which the flea market respects. Drift the stalls, flip through someone's entire record collection, climb the hill above the amphitheater where a stranger is absolutely destroying a power ballad.
rounds.title: Mauerpark Sunday

rounds.goodbye: The day is officially over. Verified.
rounds.subtitle: The release shipped, or it didn't; either way the laptop is closed. Walk it off through the warm dark — späti light, the U-Bahn rumbling somewhere under your feet, the bridge over the tracks where the city glitters like it's showing off.
rounds.title: The Late Shift

rounds.goodbye: The domes keep listening. To nothing.
rounds.subtitle: A hill made of the old city's rubble, grown over with forest, crowned with the ruined listening station's white domes. The climb is real, the history is heavier, and the view goes all the way to the TV tower.
rounds.title: Teufelsberg

rounds.goodbye: The inbox survived without you.
rounds.subtitle: The lot is half full of Subarus and the trail starts climbing before you've locked the car. Two switchbacks to quiet the head, a third to quiet the legs, and the ridge line up top holding the morning's first warm light.
rounds.title: Switchbacks

rounds.goodbye: You saw the day arrive. It saw you.
rounds.subtitle: Alarm at five-forty, no snooze, up the ridge trail half by feel with a headlamp you probably didn't need. The last pitch is steep enough to shut the brain up — then the top, the stillness, and the sun clearing the plains like it rehearsed.
rounds.title: First Light

rounds.goodbye: You made the week count.
rounds.subtitle: One week a year the grove turns entirely to light, and this is that week. The loop climbs through the white trunks, the leaves doing their applause thing in the wind, and everyone on the trail is grinning about the same secret.
rounds.title: The Aspen Loop

rounds.goodbye: Sea level will feel like cheating.
rounds.subtitle: Up here the air keeps its distance and every grade gets a promotion. Walk it anyway — slower, honester — to the overlook bench that has the entire valley memorized. The bench is earned. Sitting on it is mandatory.
rounds.title: Ten Thousand Feet

rounds.goodbye: The one-thirty can have what's left.
rounds.subtitle: The path follows the creek right through the middle of town, and the creek doesn't know about your one-thirty. Cottonwoods, the flume, a kayaker doing laps in the play wave — the mountains keeping an eye on all of it.
rounds.title: The Creek Path

rounds.goodbye: Salt air, mountains, done.
rounds.subtitle: The mountains hold the last light, the freighters sit out in the bay like patient dogs, and the seawall carries everyone — runners, roller skaters, you — around the park's long curve while the sky sorts itself out.
rounds.title: The Seawall

rounds.goodbye: La ville, d'en haut. Worth it.
rounds.subtitle: The city keeps an actual mountain in its living room. The gravel path switchbacks up under the maples, joggers in both directions, and at the top the lookout hands you the whole city — the river, the bridges, your neighborhood somewhere in it.
rounds.title: Mont Royal

rounds.goodbye: Back at street level. Softer now.
rounds.subtitle: Forty steps down from the sidewalk the city just switches off — creek, cottonwoods, a heron with a lot of patience. The ravine runs for kilometers under everyone's feet, and the climb back out is the toll it charges.
rounds.title: The Ravine

rounds.goodbye: Cheeks: frozen. Worth it: entirely.
rounds.subtitle: It started during dinner and it's actually sticking. Boots on before the plows ruin it — the streetlights full of falling static, the park's small hill gone white, your own footprints the first ones on the path.
rounds.title: First Snow

rounds.goodbye: Family: walked. Leftovers: earned.
rounds.subtitle: Too much of everything yesterday, so today the entire household gets walked like a dog. Around the block, past the rink, the family spreading into pairs and their conversations — the annual proof that fresh air fixes most of it.
rounds.title: Boxing Day

rounds.goodbye: Sunday, fulfilled. See you next week.
rounds.subtitle: The whole country is out in it — families, dogs, someone's grandmother setting an alarming pace. One long easy grade through the trees, a thermos at the halfway point, and the shared national understanding that this is simply what Sunday is.
rounds.title: Søndagstur

rounds.goodbye: The theory holds. Good jacket.
rounds.subtitle: The rain is horizontal and the locals are unbothered, so you will be unbothered too. Shell zipped to the chin, hood cinched, out along the ridge path where the weather is loudest — smug, waterproof, fully alive.
rounds.title: No Bad Weather

rounds.goodbye: The fjord will hold your place.
rounds.subtitle: The fjord holds the sky like it's being careful with it. The path rolls along the shoreline, over the headland, past the red boathouses — and the ferry crosses mid-frame exactly when the view needed it to.
rounds.title: The Fjord Path

rounds.goodbye: Stove lit. Weekend begins.
rounds.subtitle: The car only goes so far; the last stretch to the cabin is a track through the birches that climbs like it means it. Pack on, phone already useless, the week dropping off you somewhere around the second steep bit.
rounds.title: Up to the Hytte

rounds.goodbye: Back by one. Sharper than you left.
rounds.subtitle: The calendar block says 'lunsj' and everyone respects it, because everyone has their own. Out the door before someone can schedule something, up the hill behind the office at a pace that means business, back with your head rinsed clean.
rounds.title: Lunsj

rounds.goodbye: Kanelbulle: had. Balance: restored.
rounds.subtitle: Fika is not coffee; fika is the agreement that the day stops at three. The walk over is half the ritual — through the courtyard, up the rise past the water tower, arriving with cold cheeks to a warm window seat and someone glad to see you.
rounds.title: Fika at Three

rounds.goodbye: Light: collected. Winter: survivable.
rounds.subtitle: The sun clears the rooftops at ten and starts packing up by two, so when it's out, you go — no negotiating. Along the water where the light lies down flat and gold, walking fast enough to keep warm, slow enough to bank it all.
rounds.title: The Winter Light

rounds.goodbye: The spot stays secret. Yours now.
rounds.subtitle: Someone at work mentioned a spot, vaguely, the way people do when they'll never tell you the real one. Up into the mossy pines anyway — the slow, head-down hunt, the first gold flash under the spruce, the bag filling one small victory at a time.
rounds.title: Chanterelles

rounds.goodbye: The island stays. That's the deal.
rounds.subtitle: Over the bridge and the city hands you an island — royal oaks, gravel paths, water glinting on both sides. Half of Stockholm is out here doing the same slow lap, and nobody is in a hurry to finish it.
rounds.title: Djurgården

rounds.goodbye: The tomatoes noticed you came.
rounds.subtitle: The kolonilott is four hundred square meters of dirt that answers only to you. Out past the painted sheds, up the rows the hill insists on, water the tomatoes, judge the neighbor's dahlias, walk home smelling faintly of soil and superiority.
rounds.title: The Allotment

rounds.goodbye: The city, from above it all.
rounds.subtitle: The Heath pretends to be countryside and mostly gets away with it. Up the kite hill with the dogs and the determined prams, and at the top — the whole skyline at once, St Paul's to the towers, doing its trick of looking painted on.
rounds.title: Parliament Hill

rounds.goodbye: The river's seen worse days than yours.
rounds.subtitle: The tide is out and the river smells like history. Up onto the bridge with the commuter current, along the south bank as the crowds thin, the second bridge carrying you home while the water goes pewter under the lamps.
rounds.title: The Thames Path

rounds.goodbye: Mutiny complete. Back to it.
rounds.subtitle: The emails will keep; they always keep. Out past the sandwich queue and into the park's long diagonal, plane trees overhead, deckchairs full of people having the same quiet mutiny you are.
rounds.title: The Park at Lunch

rounds.goodbye: Second place. A moral victory.
rounds.subtitle: The nearest pub is fine, which is the problem — the good one is two neighborhoods over, up past the church, and the walk is part of the membership fee. They're already at the table by the window, saving your seat and mispronouncing your specialist subject.
rounds.title: The Local

rounds.goodbye: Not your dog. Still your joy.
rounds.subtitle: At this hour the common belongs to the dogs and whoever they brought with them. The light goes violet behind the old oaks, somebody's spaniel is having the best day of its life again, and the loop walks you as much as you walk it.
rounds.title: The Common at Dusk

rounds.goodbye: "Okay — no, YOU hang up." Walked and warmed.
rounds.subtitle: Some calls are too good for the couch. Headphones in, dial as the door closes behind you — laps of the neighborhood while the story gets going, and you take the hill without noticing because the other voice is mid-sentence.
rounds.title: The Call

rounds.goodbye: They'll say they're fine again next week. Go anyway.
rounds.subtitle: They said they're fine, which is how you know to go. The long blocks over with nothing in your hands but the visit itself — they'll say you needn't have come, then talk for an hour, and the walk home will feel like it mattered. Because it did.
rounds.title: Looking In

rounds.goodbye: It was gone in eleven minutes. Glory.
rounds.subtitle: You said you'd bring the good one, so now the casserole rides level the whole way or it doesn't ride at all. Steady down the long sidewalk, past two other foil-covered pilgrims headed the same direction — arriving warm is the entire assignment.
rounds.title: The Potluck

rounds.goodbye: Nothing happened. You missed nothing. Perfect.
rounds.subtitle: The phone stays in the drawer, and for the first three blocks that feels like a missing limb. Then it doesn't. The long easy way around, nothing to check, nothing checking on you — just the neighborhood, rendering in full detail for once.
rounds.title: Off Screen

rounds.goodbye: The wave, returned at the corner.
rounds.subtitle: A small hand in yours and a story with no ending, all the way up the rise. At the gate, the ritual wave. The way back is yours alone — which is exactly enough time for the park loop and the first uninterrupted thought of the day.
rounds.title: The Drop-Off
